sources.name: Cool Communities Program, Los Angeles (1997)
sources.summary: A published Los Angeles cooling package is cited in urban heat literature at roughly US$1B. It is a real cost anchor for whole-city mitigation planning, not a fabricated model output.
sources.sourceNote: Use this only as a coarse benchmark until the repo has a city-specific unit-cost table.

sources.name: Mitigating New York City's Heat Island With Urban Forestry, Living Roofs, and Light Surfaces
sources.summary: The literature-cited NYSERDA report ranks interventions by temperature reduction cost effectiveness, stating that light surfaces, light roofs, and curbside planting are cheaper per degree of cooling than street trees.
sources.sourceNote: Use this for priority ranking only. It is not a per-unit cost table.

sources.name: Cool pavement pilot program, New York City (2025)
sources.summary: Public reporting cites a cool-pavement pilot program in New York City and an incremental sealant premium of about $0.60 per square yard versus traditional sealants.
sources.sourceNote: Use as a public planning anchor and derived seed cost example only.
